findings.title: add() now subtracts: the + operator was changed to -, so add(2, 3) returns -1 instead of 5
findings.body: The return expression changed from `a + b` to `a - b`, so add() now returns the difference of its arguments, not the sum. add(2, 3) returns -1 instead of 5, add(5, 5) returns 0 instead of 10, and add(1, -1) returns 2 instead of 0. The result only matches the old behaviour when b == 0. The return type is still a number, so callers will not see a TypeError. They will quietly get wrong values, which is harder to catch than a crash. Nothing in the change suggests this was intended: the function is still called add and its signature is unchanged. Restore `return a + b` and add a test that would catch this, such as add(2, 3) == 5.
findings.evidence:
-    return a + b
+    return a - b
